thread:
ada: seeing repeated OOMs on eu-west-dedicated-3 pool for tenant `az`. started ~10:02 UTC, 4 host-level OOM kills in last hour :/

rory: can you paste the kube logs / dmesg? is it CUDA OOM or driver oom?

ada: quick tail of the pod logs and dmesg snippet:
```
I tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:xxxx] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: out of memory
kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

zara: hmm looks like fragmentation rather than single big alloc. which instance type? are we packing other tenants on same GPU?

ada: p4d. routing shows tenant `az` on dedicated-3 which is a shared-dedicated pool (we let non-enterprise spill into it during low usage). noticed co-located jobs from tenant `beta-prod` with long-lived KV cache.

matt: that matches the routing policy we enabled last month: `soft-dedicated-fallthrough=true` — cheaper but allows cross-tenant colocations when capacity is tight.

rory: we should check GPU memory usage histogram and per-tenant allocator stats. infra-bot, pull last 6h mem histogram for hosts in dedicated-3?

infra-bot: (automated) metrics query started: hosts=dedicated-3, metric=gpu_memory_usage, range=6h. ETA ~20s.

infra-bot: (automated) results: 70% of samples show >85% memory utilization on 3/8 hosts; 1 host regularly spikes to 98%.

zara: that explains the OOMs. two immediate options: 1) force tenant `beta-prod` off dedicated-3 (evict long KV jobs) or 2) convert dedicated-3 subset to strict tenant-isolation (no fallthrough). both have cost/availability tradeoffs.

ada: customer `az` SLA is impacted. requesting immediate eviction for the long-tail jobs, then we can consider isolation for the pool.

matt: eviction script exists but will cause queued backlog and may increase latency for beta-prod. cost-wise, strict isolation reduces binpacking efficiency ~12% based on last quarter.

rory: can we MIG-split the p4d GPUs for better isolation? I recall driver-level MIG support is flaky on p4d.

zara: p4d doesn't support useful MIG slices for our models (sequence lengths + kv cache). also many models rely on single-device large memory. MIG not viable here.

ada: proposed action: (1) run targeted eviction of beta-prod jobs on the 3 hot hosts (non-disruptive drain + cordon) (2) flip `soft-dedicated-fallthrough=false` for dedicated-3 and roll canary to one AZ (3) monitor 24h and roll to remaining hosts if good. if not, escalate to resizing pool.

matt: +1 to plan. estimate impact: eviction will free ~60% mem on those hosts, expected drop in OOMs. cost risk: dedicated capacity pressure may rise; we should alert capacity-ops.

rory: I'll run an infra-safe eviction with `--grace-period=120` and tag the affected jobs for priority resubmit to other pools. putting a short runbook here:
```
# eviction commands
kubectl cordon host-xyz
kubectl drain host-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# then move jobs: tag tenant beta-prod as low-priority for 6h
```

ada: tagging done. starting eviction now. will update when cordon completes. :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:

infra-bot: (automated) alert: pool dedicated-3 OOM-rate fell 82% after evictions (5m window).

zara: good signal. still want to flip `soft-dedicated-fallthrough` to false as a canary (single AZ) so we don't get surprises tonight. who owns the routing policy toggle?

matt: that's infra-team. I can do the toggle and monitor. will do canary in eu-west-1a at 11:40 UTC.

rory: also recommend a short-term quota bump for az tenant if they expect more traffic this week; avoids immediate reschedules. product needs to approve.

ada: I'll loop in product.

matt: toggled `soft-dedicated-fallthrough=false` for eu-west-1a canary at 11:40 UTC. watching traces + tailing tail_latency metric.

infra-bot: (automated) routing change deployed to canary az.

ada: initial checks: no new OOMs in 20m, latency stable. good so far. :thumbsup:

zara: plan for longer term: evaluate dedicated-reservation expansion vs smarter eviction heuristics (eviction by KV-footprint). also add allocator compaction improvements to reduce fragmentation. need input from runtime team for compaction effort estimate.

matt: I'll open a follow-up ticket for capacity/price impact analysis and link to this thread.

rory: thumbs up. also flagging possible network egress constraints if we reschedule many jobs across AZs — might need batch-throttle during reschedule window.

ada: noted. putting a short postmortem template in the ticket. thanks all, closing thread after we confirm 24h stability. :eyes:
